COURSE

STORY GAME

FOUR CHAPTERS · ONE WEEKEND · QUICK RUN UNDER 45 MIN · FULL RUN 1.5 TO 2.5 HOURS

Practise the whole hackathon weekend before the real one.

You are Shad. You came solo, with a laptop and a plan. Join a team, build through Saturday night, meet the sponsors on Sunday morning, then demo to the judges. Every choice shows up on a report card at the end.

Things the organizers haven't announced yet, like the venue, the AI-tool rule and the challenge, change every run. Play it a few times before the real thing (its date has not been announced).

Walk: arrow keys or WASD (on a phone, the pad). Talk or continue: Space, Enter or the A button. Choose: up and down, then Enter.

Pause: Esc or the Menu button: resume, settings, or save and quit. The game saves by itself at safe moments, so Continue always puts you back.

ARROWS OR WASD TO WALK · SPACE OR ENTER TO TALK · ESC TO PAUSE · F FOR FULL SCREEN

LEARN · SHORT LESSONS, THEN A TIMED FINAL TEST

Your course.

How this course is checked, and what is not
  • Run by a computer: every code example and printed result in Levels 4 to 12 is run for real (Python, Node, SQLite, scikit-learn) and run again after every change. Every lesson step is also tested through this page.
  • Read from the official docs: statements about Claude, GitHub, Docker, FastAPI and similar were checked against the provider's own pages on 23 October 2026. Model names, prices, free tiers and docs pages change, so treat them as a dated snapshot: next check due 23 November 2026.
  • Not checked by a computer: how well an explanation teaches, how hard a step is, and how long a lesson really takes. No beginner has tried Levels 4 to 12 yet, so the minutes are estimates.
  • Code you write: JavaScript and most Python steps run your code on the lesson's own examples, right here in your browser (Python is downloaded from this same site, about 12 MB, the first time you reach one). SQL, TypeScript and the few Python steps that need extra libraries cannot run in the page, so for those you compare your code with the model answer and tick what you really covered; nothing marks it for you.
  • Final tests: auto-marked questions, one try each, the answer is shown after a miss, and a reload carries on where you were. They are practice, not a certificate anyone else will check.
  • No promise: this course teaches skills. It does not promise a job, a salary or a result.
  • Found a mistake? Tell us on GitHub (free account needed).

                        LIVE CHARACTERS AND PRIYA (OPTIONAL)

                        Add a DeepSeek or OpenRouter API key and every conversation gets a Type my own answer option. The character reads what you typed and replies in their own voice, and how they react changes your scores. With a key, the green-screen terminals also become a live computer: you type real commands (ls, cat, grep, git, docker, kill) at a real hackathon emergency, and Priya's hints come from what is on screen. Without a key, the game plays exactly the same with the written choices and practice terminals.

                        API Key

                        Take the key off this computer (for example, a shared or borrowed laptop). You can paste it in again any time.

                        Are you sure? Your API key will be removed from this computer.

                        The key goes straight from this page to DeepSeek (or OpenRouter, for sk-or- keys) and nowhere else. Both run the same DeepSeek Flash model. A conversation reply costs under a tenth of a cent and a terminal command about a sixth of a cent. A Quick run costs roughly 5 to 10 cents and a Full run or long drill roughly 10 to 25 cents. The game stops after 400 replies per day as a safety cap (at most about a dollar a day). Use a key with a small balance ($5 lasts dozens of runs), and remove it before sharing this computer.
